n.sample_role: Participants in the Experiment 1 reading-time LMM. Model also includes 24 stimulus items and 4431 sentence-level reading-time observations, separately.
n.exclusions: One of 36 recruited participants excluded for technical problems; 2.33% of reading-time data removed as outliers 2.5 SD below/above each participant’s mean sentence reading time.
n.location: p. 883 (PDF article p. 7), Table 1, NPart; pp. 881–882, Experiment 1 Participants and Results/Reading times.

replication.target_description: Printed replication t-test pools all valences in code, despite narrative describing positive passages

n.sample_role: reading-time observations in third-person and second-person groups respectively
n.exclusions: Reading-time cleaning; code does not filter positive passages for this t-test

reported_success.quote: I believe that this may be considered a partial replication as my results indicate a similar trend.

notes:
The printed t-test code pools valences; target_match false despite prose claiming a positive-passage test. Primary table means also contain a unit discrepancy and were not used for this test.
Completion source review (n_o): Directly printed NPart = 35 in Table 1 for the identified Experiment 1 reading-time model. Experiment 1, perspective contrast for positive-emotion passage reading times, p. 883 below Figure 1; least-squares comparison within the reading-time LMM described on p. 882 and in Table 1. Participant N is distinct from recruitment (36), item N (24), and sentence-level observation N (4431). One participant and 2.33% of reading-time data were excluded as documented on pp. 881–882. The positive-emotion perspective test is a conditional contrast from the common LMM, with perspective manipulated within participants. The reported participant count of that model is 35; a positive-only observation count is not separately printed, and is not inferred from df.
